description.narrative: The development objective of the Msimbazi Basin Development Project for Tanzania is to strengthen flood resilience and integrated urban development in an economically important and flood prone area of the Msimbazi river basin in Dar es Salaam. The project comprises of five components. The first component, Msimbazi river basin development infrastructure provides an integrated, long-term solution to substantially reduce the impacts of floods in the lower Msimbazi river basin that will improve hydraulic capacity of the river, provide an area for flood water detention, build resiliency of key transport infrastructure, regenerate valuable land assets to control encroachment in flood prone areas and allow for public recreation and urban development, and reduce degradation of the Msimbazi watershed. It consists of following sub-components: (i) flood control interventions; (ii) resilient transport infrastructure; (iii) msimbazi city park and redevelopment area; and (iv) watershed management through greening, erosion control, and litter management. The second component, preventative resettlement will finance, the preventive resettlement of low-income flood-prone communities in the lower Msimbazi river basin and project-related displaced persons in compliance with the World Bank environmental and social framework (ESF). It consists of following sub-components: (i) resettlement compensation; and (ii) livelihood restoration. The third component, strengthening institutions for resilient urban development focuses on governance reforms, strengthening new and existing institutions, building capacity, and facilitating coordination for management of the Msimbazi river basin, including the investments and assets created under the project, the surrounding urban area, and the watershed. It consists of following sub-components: (i) Msimbazi special planning area (MSPA) institutional strengthening; (ii) Msimbazi river basin management institutional strengthening; and (iii) local government authorities institutional strengthening. The fourth component, project management will finance the direct costs of management and operation of the project to ensure smooth delivery and compliance with World Bank policy and guidelines. The fifth component, contingent emergency response finance, inter alia provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed. This component enables rapid response to eligible emergencies and disasters caused by natural and man-made events by providing contingent financing.
To strengthen flood resilience and integrated urban development in an economically important and flood prone area of the Msimbazi river basin in Dar es Salaam.

condition.narrative: Section I.A. 2 of the Schedule to the Project Agreement:TANROADS shall, by no later than three (3) months after the effectivenessselect and appoint, in the its Project Implementation Team, one (1) additional procurement specialist and two (2) additionalaccountants, all of them with qualification and experience and under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.A.1(a) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:Government of Tanzania to establish, by not later than six months aftereffectiveness, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project, a Project Steering Committee, with amandate, terms of reference, composition, and resources satisfactory to the Association, to provide policy guidance, high-leveloversight and strategic advice and support for the carrying out of the Project

Section I.D.1 & 2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement and Section I.C1 of the Schedule to the Project Agreement:Government ofTanzania and TANROADS to prepared and furnish to the Association, by no later than March 31 of each year, an annual work plan andbudget for the Project for the subsequent fiscal year, of such scope and detail as the Association shall have reasonably requested.

Section I.E.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:Government of Tanzania to prepare and furnish to the Association, by notlater than three six (6) months after the effectiveness, a time bound Msimbazi basin development program action plan for theMsimbazi Special Planning Area, outlining the sequencing, deadlines, procedural steps and allocation of responsibilities for theachievement and/or implementation of the milestones and activities therein identified, all in a manner and substance satisfactoryto the Association.

Section I.G.5 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall, by not later than three (3) months after the EffectiveDate, through the Dar es Salaam City Council Project Implementation Team, select, engage/hire and thereafter maintain throughoutthe period of implementation of the Project, the services of a supervision and coordination consulting firm/organization, withqualifications and experience and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association, in order to assist the Dar es Salaam CityCouncil Project Implementation Team with the carrying out of the resettlement activities under the Project, including thecertification of Land Acquisition & Resettlements Compensations payments, the timely response to any grievances raised inconnection therewith, and, whenever applicable, the certification of contractors compliance with/implementation of theResettlement Policy Framework and Resettlement Action Plan.
